content.title: Media Queries: Change the Rules When Needed
content.hook: Sometimes the relationship itself should change when there is less room.
content.context: CSS media queries let you apply different rules under a condition.

content.title: A simple condition

content.question: At 900px wide, which `grid-template-columns` rule should describe the layout?

options.text: The one-column rule inside the media query.

feedback.correct: The condition `(max-width: 700px)` is false at 900px, so the media query rule does not apply there.
feedback.incorrect: Check the condition `(max-width: 700px)`: 900px is wider than 700px, so the media query block is inactive and the base three-column rule remains in effect.

content.question: At 600px wide, what is the intended result?

options.text: The media query condition is true, so the one-column rule can apply.
The page must use three columns.

feedback.correct: 600px satisfies `max-width: 700px`, so the alternate layout rule becomes active.
feedback.incorrect: At 600px wide, the condition `(max-width: 700px)` is true, so the `.cards` rule inside the `@media` block overrides `grid-template-columns` with `1fr`.

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Add a `@media (max-width: 700px)` rule that switches `.cards` to a single column (`grid-template-columns: 1fr;`), then run the preview.

content.prompt:
The `.cards` grid starts with three columns (`repeat(3, 1fr)`), which feels cramped inside this narrower preview viewport.

Without changing the HTML, complete the `@media (max-width: 700px)` block by setting `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` on `.cards`, then run the preview to see the layout switch to a single column.
content.htmlFixture:
1. Base Rule

Uses three columns when wide space is available.

2. Condition

Checks whether viewport width is at or below 700px.

3. Adapted Rule

Stacks into a single readable column when narrow.

testCases.description: Keeps `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);` on the base `.cards` rule

feedback.correct: Your stylesheet keeps the base 3-column rule and overrides `.cards` with `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` inside `@media (max-width: 700px)`. Because the preview viewport is under 700px wide, the single-column rule is now active.
feedback.incorrect: Keep `grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);` on the base `.cards` rule and set `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` inside `@media (max-width: 700px) { .cards { ... } }` so the layout switches to one column at narrower widths.

content.title: Breakpoint reasoning
content.text:
The number 700px is not sacred.

It is a design choice based on where the current layout stops fitting well.

A different content set might need a different threshold.

A useful breakpoint answers a real question:

**“At what point should the relationship change?”**

content.question: What is a media query really doing here?

options.text: Applying a different CSS rule when a condition about the environment is true.
Changing the meaning of the document.

feedback.correct: The media query does not change the document's meaning. It changes which presentation rule is active under a condition.
feedback.incorrect: Media queries never alter HTML tags or document meaning—they conditionally apply CSS presentation rules when an environment test such as `(max-width: 700px)` is true.

activities.title: Replicate UI: Responsive Media-Query Card Stack
activities.instruction: Complete the `@media (max-width: 500px)` rule so `.plan-grid` switches from 3 cramped columns to a single readable column (`1fr`) in the 360px mobile viewport.

content.prompt: In the 360px mobile viewport, `.plan-grid` is currently squeezed into `repeat(3, 1fr)`. Inside `@media (max-width: 500px)`, override `.plan-grid` with `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` so the cards stack cleanly.
hints: Keep the base `.plan-grid` rule for wide viewports (`display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr); gap: 10px;`).

structuralRules.feedbackOnFail: Keep all 3 <article class="plan-card"> items inside <section class="plan-grid">.

styleRules.feedbackOnFail: Add `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` to `.plan-grid` inside `@media (max-width: 500px)` so it switches to one column at 360px.

feedback.correct: Because the stage viewport is 360px wide (`<= 500px`), your `@media (max-width: 500px)` rule overrides `.plan-grid` from three cramped columns to a clean single-column stack.
feedback.incorrect: `.plan-grid` is still using three columns at 360px. Add `grid-template-columns: 1fr;` inside `@media (max-width: 500px) { .plan-grid { ... } }`.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** A media query is a condition that can change presentation rules.
**Senior habit:** Pick a breakpoint because the layout needs to change, not because a device category told you to.
**Mastery signal:** You can explain why a rule is active or inactive at a given width.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
